item.description: A proper wet winter weekend concentrates everything. The answer on a day like this is one indoor booking with some real weight to it - truffle country, a long lunch, or the pools when the air outside is genuinely cold.

item.title: Peninsula This Weekend - 4 to 5 July
item.description: The first full school-holiday weekend of winter is simple: one booked truffle hunt, one Sunday heritage train run, and one indoor family plan that does not feel like a fallback.

item.title: Peninsula This Weekend - 27 to 28 June
item.description: The solstice crowd has gone home. This is the quiet winter weekend of truffle hunts, local markets, and the final Sunday Sessions at the springs.

item.title: Peninsula This Weekend - 20 to 21 June
item.description: The solstice weekend moves from Sorrento's festival foreshore on Saturday to the stillness of the springs and the forest on Sunday.

item.title: The Sorrento Solstice Festival: A Night When the Peninsula Burns
item.description: The longest night of the year deserves a proper send-off. Two days on the Sorrento foreshore, a six-metre effigy on the bay, and the particular magic of a winter festival done right.

item.title: Peninsula This Weekend - 13 to 14 June
item.description: The week after King's Birthday: truffle season at its most available, cellar doors open and unhurried, and the Peninsula genuinely itself again.

item.title: Peninsula Notes - June 2026
item.description: Truffle season begins on the ridge. The fog is back most mornings. Flinders is doing something unusual for a coastal town in winter: it is full.

item.title: The One Booking Peninsula Day
item.description: Most Peninsula days are over-planned. The ones that work usually aren't. One table, one walk, one decision made in the morning about which direction the rest of the day will go.

item.title: Why the Peninsula Works Better in Winter
item.description: Empty dining rooms, cheaper rooms, and the particular quality of light that makes the ridge look like a different country. The case for coming in July rather than January.

item.title: Peninsula This Weekend - 6 to 7 June
item.description: King's Birthday is the loudest winter weekend on the Peninsula. Two clear moves, and the rest of the weekend kept open.

item.title: Peninsula This Weekend - 30 to 31 May
item.description: Autumn closes and winter opens on the same patch of Main Ridge on Saturday: the Peninsula marking its own calendar.

item.title: Peninsula This Weekend - 23 to 24 May
item.description: The Saturday markets are dark and truffle season is a week away: what's left is the Peninsula in its most deliberate register.

item.title: Peninsula This Weekend - 16 to 17 May
item.description: Mid-May gives the Peninsula back to itself. One forest morning, one market Sunday, nothing that needs to be organised beyond that.

item.title: Peninsula This Weekend - 9 to 10 May
item.description: Mother's Day is the organising principle. Book lunch first, then let the rest of the weekend behave.

item.title: Dromana: The Peninsula Insider Guide
item.description: Dromana is the Peninsula's practical gateway - a bay town at the foot of Arthurs Seat with easier edges than the famous villages further south. Come when you want a base that can do beach, ridge and family logistics without pretending to be something rarer than it is.

item.title: Flinders: The Peninsula Insider Guide
item.description: Flinders is the quiet southern village that proves the Peninsula does not need theatre to be good. Come for the harder light, the ocean edge, and a day shaped by a walk, a bakery and one proper lunch rather than a schedule full of noise.

item.title: Main Ridge: The Peninsula Insider Guide
item.description: Main Ridge is the Peninsula's highest, coolest and most wine-serious pocket - less a village than a plateau of good decisions. Come when you want the Peninsula stripped back to vineyards, fog, lunch and roads lined with trees rather than distractions.

item.title: Merricks: The Peninsula Insider Guide
item.description: Merricks is the understated corridor between bay and ridge where the Peninsula's wine country starts to feel private. Come for the general store, the estates, the pub and the rare pleasure of a district that seems to know exactly how little fuss it needs.

item.title: Mornington: The Peninsula Insider Guide
item.description: Mornington is the Peninsula's commercial hub, but that undersells it badly. Done properly, it is the best entry point for first-timers - a town with enough main-street life, foreshore access and market culture to explain the region before you drive any further south.

item.title: Portsea: The Peninsula Insider Guide
item.description: Portsea is the Peninsula's quiet final note - more private than Sorrento, less immediately legible, and better for visitors who already know how to read the tip. Come for Point Nepean, the back beaches and one of the most withheld village atmospheres in Victoria.

item.title: Red Hill: The Peninsula Insider Guide
item.description: Red Hill is the Peninsula's food-and-wine centre of gravity, but the best version of it is narrower than most visitors think. This is a place for one market morning, one properly chosen cellar door, and one lunch that gets the whole day.

item.title: Sorrento: The Peninsula Insider Guide
item.description: Sorrento is the Peninsula at its most legible - limestone, tide, old money, and a main street that still works once the holiday theatre clears. Come in the off-season, stay two nights, and use it as a real town rather than a summer errand.
